{{short description|American statistician}}
'''Karen Kafadar''' is an American statistician. She is Commonwealth Professor of Statistics at the [[University of Virginia]], and chair of the statistics department there. She was editor-in-chief of ''[[Technometrics]]'' from 1999 to 2001,{{r|40ytm}} and was president of the [[International Association for Statistical Computing]] for 2011–2013.{{r|iasc}}
In 2017 she was elected president of the [[American Statistical Association]] for the 2019 term.{{r|elpres}}

==Education and career==
Kafadar earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and a master's degree in statistics from [[Stanford University]], both in 1975.{{r|elpres|cv}}
She completed her PhD in statistics from [[Princeton University]] in 1979 under the supervision of [[John Tukey]]; her dissertation was ''Robust Confidence Intervals for the One- and Two- Sample Problem''.{{r|elpres|cv|mgp}}
Before moving to the University of Virginia in 2014, Kafadar was Rudy Professor of Statistics at [[Indiana University]]. She has also worked for the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]], [[Hewlett Packard]], the [[National Cancer Institute]], the [[University of Colorado Denver]], and [[Oregon State University]].{{r|elpres|cv}}

==Awards and honors==
Kafadar is a [[fellow]] of the American Statistical Association (since 1994) and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2012), and an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] (2007).{{r|elpres|cv}} In 2023 Kafadar was recipient of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award|American Statistical Association's Founders Award]].{{r|ASAFoundersAward}}
